title: Parse a CSV line
summary: Split one CSV record into fields, honouring quotes, commas and doubled quotes.
prompt: An export tool hands you CSV one line at a time and you cannot use the `csv` module in this
sandbox. Write `parse_csv_line(line: str) -> list[str]` for RFC 4180 style CSV:
- Fields are separated by commas. Empty fields are kept: `"a,,c,"` -> `["a", "", "c", ""]`.
- A field that **starts** with `"` is quoted: it runs to the matching closing quote and may contain commas.
- Inside a quoted field, `""` stands for one `"` character.
- A `"` in the middle of an unquoted field is just a character: `12" pizza` stays `12" pizza`.
- An empty line is one empty field: `[""]`.
- A quoted field with no closing quote raises `ValueError`.
template: Dojo.eq("a comma inside quotes", ["1", "Smith, Jane", "NY"], parse_csv_line('1,"Smith, Jane",NY'))
Dojo.eq("doubled quotes become one quote", ['She said "hi"', "x"], parse_csv_line('"She said ""hi""",x'))
Dojo.eq("empty fields, including the last", ["a", "", "c", ""], parse_csv_line("a,,c,"))
Dojo.eq("a quote inside an unquoted field is literal", ['12" pizza', "9.99"], parse_csv_line('12" pizza,9.99'))
Dojo.eq("an empty line is one empty field", [""], parse_csv_line(""))
Dojo.throws("an unterminated quote raises ValueError", ValueError, lambda: parse_csv_line('"abc,d'))

forbid.message: Does not use the csv module

hints: Scan character by character and remember whether you are at the start of a field.
A quote only opens a quoted field at the start of a field. Inside one, look ahead: `""` is a literal quote, a single `"` closes it.
Append the last field after the loop, even when it is empty; that is how `"a,"` gives two fields.
